title: Raita

ingredients.title: For the Yogurt Base
items: Thick yogurt (dahi) – 500 g (about 2 cups), full-fat and unsweetened
Chilled water or milk – 2–3 tbsp (optional, for a thinner consistency)

ingredients.title: For the Vegetables & Herbs
items: Cucumber – 1 medium, peeled, deseeded, and finely diced or grated
Onion – ½ small, very finely minced (optional)
Tomato – ½ medium, deseeded and finely diced (optional)
Fresh coriander leaves – 2 tbsp, finely chopped
Fresh mint leaves – 1 tbsp, finely chopped
Green chili – 1 small, deseeded and very finely minced (optional)

instruction.title: Prepare the Yogurt Base
steps: Place the thick yogurt in a mixing bowl.
Whisk until completely smooth and lump-free.
For a lighter consistency, whisk in 2–3 tbsp chilled water or milk.

instruction.title: Prepare the Vegetables
steps: Peel and deseed the cucumber to reduce excess moisture.
Finely dice or grate the cucumber.
Deseed and finely dice the tomato if using.
Finely mince the onion and green chili if using.

instruction.title: Combine & Season
steps: Add cucumber, tomato, onion, coriander, and mint to the whisked yogurt.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and regular salt.
Mix gently until the vegetables and herbs are evenly distributed.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.

instruction.title: Chill & Serve
steps: Cover the raita and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Transfer to a chilled serving bowl.
Garnish with a light dusting of roasted cumin powder and a fresh mint sprig.

chefTips: Extra creaminess: Strain the yogurt through muslin cloth for about 30 minutes before whisking.
Cucumber: Deseed cucumber before adding it to prevent the raita from becoming watery.
Mint: Lightly bruise the mint leaves before chopping to release their natural oils and aroma.
Seasoning: Combining black salt with a small amount of regular salt creates a deeper restaurant-style flavor.
Presentation: Serve chilled with a light cumin dusting and fresh mint for a clean, refined finish.
Pairing: Raita works especially well with biryani, kebabs, pulao, and spicy curries as a cooling accompaniment.
